title: Andorhal
timelinePosition: Directly after Chapter 6. Same day as the Ch6 close: the four riders reach Andorhal late on day 5, by the southern/back approach, after Arthas's dismissal. Scene 1 runs late in the day, Scene 2 late afternoon into dusk, Scene 3 evening of the same night. The chapter ends hours before the ambush Chapter 8 opens on.
openLocation: Andorhal: horses stabled outside the wall, then the gate, the market district and the militia post by the market gate; the granary district, a secondary granary and the inspection offices/mage quarter beyond.
transport: Arrive on Thalassian horses and stable them outside the wall; on foot inside the city.
immediateObjective: Get into Andorhal under cover, learn how the plague is being planted at the city's center, and map the cult traffic moving it.
constraints: Limited third, absolute: Sylvanas only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, feel, read or infer. Jaina's half of the day (inspection offices, mage-side access) happens offstage and arrives only as report in Scene 3.

Sylvanas reads rooms as ground: exits, cover, sightlines, gait, who is trained and who is tired. Politics turns into terrain in her head. Inner voice argues in short semicolon clauses; aloud she is finished and sure. She names no feelings.
Address: aloud Sylvanas still says 'Mage', or 'Proudmoore' in front of others. Interior she thinks 'Jaina' plainly (outline: she can think the name now). Lyriel says 'Jaina'; Cyndia does not.

Jaina's body (carried from Ch2-6): right hand dead, left hand raw with two usable fingertips. She cannot write. The outline's 'Jaina's neat notes' MUST be resolved: Corin (or Sylvanas) scribes at her dictation, or she works from spoken memory and spell-light marks. See plannerWarning on B6.
The cover paperwork is a Farstrider pass Sylvanas wrote for Jaina under her own seal (outline). Sylvanas writes it; do not have Jaina sign anything.

Jaina's sensitivity is the only way the party perceives contamination. Near the granaries and the mage quarter she should read heavy, unlike the 'nothing' she got off the tally-man in Ch6. Sylvanas sees the result in Jaina's body, not in a reading she can verify.

Tone of reliance: practical and dry. No warm trust language beyond plain working reliance. The partnership is not softened; it is harder to pull apart. Do not state the trust aloud; show it in the split and the handoff.

Havel reads as a harried, territorial, city-first captain. The party takes him at face value; the tally-man sent them to him and Sylvanas may notice that only as far as the outline allows (route-pushing 'feels wrong' without proof). He is NOT narrated as cult-paid. Ch8 reconciles. Sylvanas's unfairness to slow humans is in her head and she knows it.
Corin is nervous, over-prepared and actually excellent. He earns his place by being right and by moving toward the danger. He is not comic relief.
Andorhal is a working mill city, not a dead one: grain dust, warm dry sweetness, constant labor noise, practical low walls, wagons, clerks. Grain traffic is under new scrutiny at the gate.
No counted time in dialogue ('two breaths', 'an hour'). Orders by event: 'until I call', 'when the lamp goes out'. (Voice sheet rule.)
No Kel'Thuzad naming. No certainty the Barovs built the cult; Barov paper is connection, not guilt. Do not re-explain the lost day or the Barov name.

Do not hand Jaina the 'answering chamber' model or low/high-fidelity (that is Ch9-12). Ch7-8 rung on her ladder: layered design, live monitoring, handler-directed obedience, and the loudest signature is not the whole mechanism. B6 may state: carrier layer applied at packaging, body finishes the work. Nothing about how death becomes undeath.

The old carter and the newer grain-man clue stay background and weak. The farewell is not mentioned or solved. Cyndia's turned head is held for Ch9; do not stage her reacting to anything farewell-shaped.
Neral is not present (northbound warning line).
Lyriel is alive through this chapter; give her small, specific competence on the perimeter without foreshadowing her death on the page.
Do not collapse the partnership into overt warmth. Do not add proof that the wider spread is complete.

povKnowsAtOpen: Grain is carrying the poison, and every trail of rot still leads toward Andorhal.
Millhaven was the first village fully taken. Too much of the country beyond it shows the same weapon hidden inside ordinary sickness.
Jaina can feel the plague before local officials know what they are looking at, but they are still chasing shipments that already landed instead of stopping the spread at its source.
Barov names keep showing up in the paperwork, but a name on a deed is not guilt.
The farewell heard twice, from the old carter and the tally-man, is thin, unresolved, and not worth turning away from Andorhal for.
Arthas heard the warning and chose the war everyone could see.
A granary tally-man told them to ask for Captain Havel at the militia post by the market gate.
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: How the poison is worked into grain inside a working trade hub.
What the living body adds after ingestion that the grain alone cannot explain.
How many hidden cultists operate in Andorhal.
Whether the Barovs built this, helped it, or are only useful cover for someone else's work.
Who designed the plague or who sits above the cult.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: No Kel'Thuzad naming in this chapter.
No certainty that the Barovs built the plague cult.
No suggestion that the old carter or the newer grain-man clue is solved.
No warm trust language beyond plain working reliance.
No proof that the wider spread is already complete.
No narrated fact that Havel is cult-paid.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Andorhal is a working mill city, not an already-dead one.
The poison is worked into the grain during packaging by skilled alchemical and necromantic hands.
The granary district hides cultists, not random saboteurs: at least eight, in two layers (handlers running dead drops, masked workers contaminating grain).
The masked crew protect themselves from the grain, not from dust.
Corin has earned his place with them.
Havel keeps trying to drag the problem back into militia habits and onto routes he controls, and something about that pull feels wrong.
They can still take someone alive that night, at the secondary granary.

pov: She opens thinking Andorhal can be solved like a Farstrider hunt: scout harder, find the weak gate, read the ground better than the people who live there.
That approach stops being enough the moment the city closes around the problem. Too many clerks, too many rules, too many mages, too much grain moving under ordinary hands.
She keeps looking for the clean field answer and keeps finding only half of one.
The full picture only starts to hold when the work splits and Jaina takes the doors Sylvanas cannot open by stealth or force.
By chapter close, Sylvanas cannot pretend Jaina is just extra help. She needs Jaina's half of the hunt to make the raid possible.

beats: Jaina already proved useful on the road, but she was easier to trust when Sylvanas could watch every step of the work.
In Andorhal, Jaina keeps finding answers Sylvanas cannot pull out of streets, roofs, or frightened faces, and she does it without showing off or asking leave.
Sylvanas can think Jaina's name plainly now. What distance remains comes from caution and pressure, not contempt.

team.label: Partnership / team
beats: The group still moves at Sylvanas's pace, but the reliance is growing and neither woman bothers to name it.
The work truly splits here. Each has to trust the other to finish the part she cannot watch herself.
Keep the respect practical and dry, never sentimental.
They are not softened. They are simply harder to pull apart from the same job.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: still with the scouting pack.
Lyriel: still with the scouting pack and alive through this chapter.
Corin: introduced here as a local Kirin Tor contact inside Andorhal.

Captain Havel: introduced here at the militia post by the market gate, where the tally-man on the road sent them, as a local militia contact whose city-first caution, need for control, and habit of steering people through his own routes will obstruct the raid and may hide something worse.
Neral: not present. She remains on the northbound warning line after escorting the survivor girl out in Chapter 3.
The old carter and the newer grain-man clue: background only. Keep them weak and unresolved.

Next chapter starts: Chapter 8 opens the same night in Andorhal with Corin inside their circle, Havel pushing for a slower, cleaner move through routes he controls, and the ambush going forward anyway.

factsLocked: Andorhal is a working mill city, not another dead village.
The contamination is introduced during packaging by skilled dark alchemy and necromancy, and the cult protects itself from its own weapon during handling.
The granary district holds a hidden cult network with at least eight people in it and two layers to its command.
Corin is a trusted local ally inside Andorhal. Havel knows the city and keeps trying to steer the operation into routes he controls.
The next move is a same-night capture of a living zealot at the secondary granary.
The old carter and the newer grain-man clue remain weak, background, and unresolved.
factsNotEarned: Proof that the wider spread is already complete.
Any collapse of the partnership into overt warmth.

scenes.title: Into the Mouth
scenes.sceneFunction: They get through Andorhal's gate under cover and gather enough local truth to stop circling and start moving.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Horses stabled outside the wall. The party approaches the gate on foot with Jaina's cover paperwork, a Farstrider pass Sylvanas wrote for her under her own seal. Late on day 5; Arthas's dismissal behind them; Havel's name from the tally-man; grain is carrying the poison and every trail leads here. Jaina is exhausted, right hand dead, left raw.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas arrives believing a hunt can solve a city. The gate and the paper trail are the first hint that scouting harder will not be enough.
scenes.enrichment: Local canon: Andorhal is the agricultural nerve center, built around granaries, loading yards, manifests, wagons and clerks, with grain dust everywhere, warm dry sweetness, constant labor noise and practical low walls (lordaeron-and-northrend.md). Era-appropriate texture: grain-trade towns ran on tally sticks, bills of lading and seal impressions; a customs gate would check weights, seals and consignors. Thalassian horses settle near arcane hum (thalassian-horses.md); stabling outside the wall is a deliberate choice for mounts that draw eyes. Sources: local canon files plus general medieval grain-trade knowledge; no web fetch needed.

beats.goal: Get the party through Andorhal's gate on the cover pass without showing what they are here for, and take a first read of how the city is guarding itself.
beats.conflict: The checks are tighter than a normal trade stop: clerks take names, inspect seals and ask sharp questions about granary business, with wagons stacking behind. Sylvanas cannot tell whether the pressure is officials finally noticing the sickness or the cult tightening its own screen, nor which clerks are merely overworked and which belong to the cult. She is reading a gate like a hunt (weak point, watch pattern) and the gate answers with paperwork.

outcome.summary: They are admitted on the pass, Jaina carrying the paper answers flatly, but the grain district is already watching itself harder than it should and Sylvanas does not know who is watching.

beats.goal: Pull usable local truth out of Havel and Corin fast enough to stop circling the problem and start moving.
beats.conflict: The two men hold the problem from opposite sides and each has already been failed by an institution. Havel has the street truth but frames it in militia terms; Corin has the paper truth but has been ignored by Dalaran. Neither knows who directs the disciplined workers, and Sylvanas cannot yet tell whether Havel is merely cautious or steering them.

outcome.summary: Havel gives street truth (sickness clustering around certain granaries, supplier routes changed three months ago, workers who move like soldiers); Corin gives paper truth (tainted shipments, copied route marks, granary records Dalaran ignored). It is enough to act on, but it arrives in two halves.

Writer needs a one-line cause (he files his flagged shipment notices through Havel's post, or the post is the only door in Andorhal where Dalaran paper gets read). Also: two exposition-heavy beats open the chapter. Keep B1 gate pressure physical and B2 conversational friction (the men interrupt, disagree on scale) so it is not a briefing.

scenes.title: The Split
scenes.sceneFunction: The city forces the investigation to divide, and Sylvanas catches the human side of the cult in motion.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Late afternoon. Havel and Corin have given the street truth and the paper truth. Jaina has access Corin can open. Sylvanas has a street guide she does not fully trust. They know supplier routes changed three months ago and workers move like soldiers.
scenes.arcPressure: The clean field answer fails: Sylvanas reads the district perfectly as ground and still gets only half the picture. The split is the first time she depends on Jaina's offstage work.
scenes.enrichment: Local canon: Jaina should feel the wrongness in the grain itself; Sylvanas should read the logistics and the embedded human network (lordaeron-and-northrend.md). Tradecraft texture: dead drops use fixed cracks, loose bricks or chalk marks; handlers and workers separate so capture of one layer does not unravel the other. Masked, gloved handling of a reagent is an accepted tell of a workforce that knows the substance is hostile to the handlers. Sources: local canon plus general tradecraft knowledge.

beats.emotion: Irritation at being the one who needs another's skill, kept under a command voice; the cold fact of sending Jaina out of sight.
beats.dilemma: Keep Jaina where she can be watched, or send her through the inspection offices and mage-side doors that Sylvanas would only slow down, on the word of a clerk-mage they met an hour ago.
beats.decision: She splits the work by skill, not rank: Jaina takes Corin and the mage-side access through the inspection offices, Sylvanas takes Havel into the granary district on foot. The pack divides without discussion and Jaina does not insult them both by arguing.

beats.conflict: Havel's local knowledge is real (names, shifts, the three-month supplier changes) but he keeps steering the walk onto routes he controls, away from some lanes. Eight-plus people in the district move wrong, too disciplined, often in pairs, and the district is a maze of loading lanes with blind corners and ordinary labor noise to hide in.

outcome.summary: She stops reading the district as random sickness and starts reading it as a guarded operation with at least eight disciplined people. She also marks that Havel's help bends toward his own routes, and cannot tell if he is territorial or covering.

beats.conflict: Tailing a trained handler through three streets of lanes she does not know; no easy cover; any glance back from him or a lookout on the roof ends the hunt and warns the cell. She must also keep Havel and her own pack out of the picture.

outcome.summary: She tails him to a secondary granary and, from a rooftop, sees masked, gloved workers under lamplight handling grain: a cell with two layers (handlers running dead drops, workers contaminating grain). Proof of a live network, but she cannot rule out that she was spotted.

scenes.title: The Full Picture
scenes.sceneFunction: Jaina brings the magical answer, Sylvanas brings the physical answer, and together they choose a same-night grab.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Evening at a safe meeting point, both halves returning at once. Sylvanas has the rooftop view of the secondary granary and at least eight disciplined people; Jaina has the inspection-office and mage-quarter findings. Havel and Corin are present.
scenes.arcPressure: By the end Sylvanas cannot pretend Jaina is extra help. The raid exists only because both halves exist.
scenes.enrichment: Local canon: plague-mechanism.md. The Ch7-8 rung of Jaina's ladder is layered design, live monitoring, handler-directed obedience, and the loudest signature is not the whole mechanism; carrier layer plus body participation is already on the Ch4-6 rung. B6 stays inside that: no answering-chamber model, no fidelity talk, no source named. Sources: stories/the-plague-road/plans/plague-mechanism.md.

beats.goal: Trade her half for Jaina's and fit them into one picture of how the poison gets into the grain.
beats.conflict: Two vocabularies, one table, little time. Jaina's answer is magical and partial; Sylvanas's is physical and partial; neither explains the other until laid side by side. Jaina arrives drained from the day's work.

outcome.summary: The halves fit. Jaina: the grain is treated at packaging with a necromantic carrier layer, and the body finishes the work after it is eaten. Sylvanas: masked workers, dead drops, a treatment site, a disciplined cell. The poison is worked in by skilled alchemical and necromantic hands, and the conspiracy is visible at last. Keep the exchange to a few lines.
